questions.question: What does `app.MapOpenApi()` do?
options: Renders an interactive Swagger UI page
Exposes a machine-readable JSON document describing your API's endpoints at /openapi/v1.json
questions.explanation: MapOpenApi() (paired with AddOpenApi()) generates and serves the raw OpenAPI JSON specification, built from inspecting your existing endpoint registrations. Swagger UI is a separate layer that renders this document nicely.

questions.question: What's the relationship between the OpenAPI document and Swagger UI?
options: The OpenAPI document is the raw JSON description; Swagger UI is an interactive webpage that reads and renders that document for humans to browse and try
Swagger UI generates the OpenAPI document
You need Swagger UI even if you don't want the JSON document
questions.explanation: OpenAPI is the data format/standard. Swagger UI is one particular tool that consumes an OpenAPI document and presents it as a clickable, testable web page.

questions.question: Why is Swagger UI usually wrapped in `if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())`?
options: It only works during development for technical reasons
You typically don't want to expose an interactive 'try any endpoint' console on a real production server
Production servers can't run Swagger UI
questions.explanation: An interactive API console is a useful development tool but a potential security/exposure concern in production — most teams restrict it to non-production environments.

questions.question: What does adding `.WithSummary("...")` and `.Produces<Student>(200)` to an endpoint registration change about how the endpoint behaves at runtime?
options: Nothing about runtime behavior — it only enriches the generated OpenAPI documentation with human-readable text and expected response shapes
It changes the HTTP status code returned
It makes the endpoint require authentication
questions.explanation: These are purely documentation annotations. The endpoint's actual behavior is unchanged — only what Swagger UI (and other OpenAPI-consuming tools) display about it improves.

questions.question: Generating an OpenAPI document requires manually writing a separate description of every endpoint, duplicating your route definitions.
questions.explanation: AddOpenApi() inspects your EXISTING endpoint registrations (routes, parameter types, etc.) automatically — you don't duplicate anything; you can optionally enrich the auto-generated result with methods like WithSummary.
